value: wild-caught feral frogs were attracted to chemical stimuli from a newt (Taricha granulosa) held in a mesh pouch rather than deterred, in short 10-minute choice tests
units: categorical (time in aquarium zone next to newt pouch, centre, or away)

source.authors: David Anderson, Olivia Cervantez, Gary M. Bucciarelli, Max R. Lambert, Megan R. Friesen
source.title: Feral frogs, native newts, and chemical cues: identifying threats from and management opportunities for invasive African Clawed Frogs in Washington state

method: behavioural: two-choice aquarium test, mesh pouch with a newt versus an empty mesh pouch (sham control), time in zones scored over 10 min, linear mixed-effects model with Tukey post hoc tests
conditions: Feral X. laevis captured from stormwater ponds in Lacey and Issaquah, Washington, and housed in a captive facility (holding time not stated); each animal randomly selected from the husbandry facility. 50 choice tests in a 38 L aquarium with 2 L aged tap water, 25 with the newt pouch on the southwest side and 25 on the northeast side to rule out side cues; the other pouch was empty. The number of individual frogs and whether any were reused is not stated. Newts were wild-collected rough-skinned newts held at least two weeks and agitated for one minute before trials. Zones: next to the newt, Centre (middle fifth) and Away (the empty-pouch section and the section adjacent to it). Results pieces: Tukey post hoc tests found all pairwise comparisons significant; Newt vs Away p = 0.003; mean time Away 210.6 s (+/- 4.9 s SE) and next to the newt 368.5 s (+/- 5.1 s SE) (zone areas unequal; means not used as the value). The same paper's tadpole experiment (Rana aurora tadpoles) is a separate result and is not part of this value. Stimulus is a live newt in a pouch; no concentration of chemical measured.
quote: However, our short-duration experiments found that X. laevis were attracted to newt chemical stimuli rather than deterred.

value: free-ranging white storks approached unmown fields sprayed from an ultralight aircraft with a green leaf volatile mix ((Z)-3-hexenal, (Z)-3-hexenol, hexenyl acetate, the smell of freshly cut grass)
units: categorical (stork approaches to sprayed fields; chi-square)

source.authors: Martin Wikelski, Michael Quetting, Yachang Cheng, Wolfgang Fiedler, Andrea Flack, Anna Gagliardo, Reyes Salas, Nora Zannoni, Jonathan Williams
source.title: Smell of green leaf volatiles attracts white storks to freshly cut meadows

method: field experiment: aircraft-sprayed green leaf volatile mix on unmown fields, with plane-only and water-spray controls, stork approaches observed from the air and the ground
conditions: Free-ranging wild storks of one village population (roughly 70 individuals, Boehringen, Germany), some carrying GPS tags; no animal handled in the experiment. Four independent spray trials (monitored area 5 x 6 km, 49 storks present on 27 Apr 2018 and 37 on 2 Jul 2018) drew 9 independently approaching individuals or groups from 0.5 to 1.2 km away (pieces of the Results); only the combined total is reported, not per trial. Controls: the ultralight plane alone, or water sprayed from it, did not elicit any reactions in storks residing at the same or shorter distances (Results piece); chi-square comparison with the volatile spray, chi2 = 11.7, N = 15, df = 2, p = 0.003 (tool summary). Storks outside the 45 degree downwind band did not approach (n = 7) and storks upwind of a field never approached (tool summary). A separate single trial with a truckload of cut grass drew 3 approaching individuals or groups, which left after about 10 min when no food was found. Spray dose and concentration at the stork were not measured. Order: observation of natural mowing, then the grass trial, then the spray trials.
quote: Furthermore, uncut fields that were sprayed with a green leaf volatile organic compound mix ((Z)-3-hexenal, (Z)-3-hexenol, hexenyl acetate), the smell of freshly cut grass, immediately attracted storks.
